title: I vibe-coded Grand Theft World with DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017: a GTA-like sandbox with the entire real Earth as its map
author: poppear
selftext:
I've been experimenting with AI-assisted game development, and this is my latest project: **GTW (Grand Theft World)**.

It's an open-world sandbox where the map is the entire real Earth.

You can spawn anywhere, walk, run, jump, steal cars, drive through traffic, and fly a variety of aircraft, from a Cessna to a 747, F/A-18, Concorde, SR-71, and even Starship.

The game integrates real-world datasets:

* Terrain and elevation data
* OpenStreetMap roads and buildings
* Satellite imagery
* Live weather, including its effects on driving and movement physics

I built it using **DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017**, starting from FableFlight, an existing vibe-coded open-source flight simulator. Full credit to its original author for the foundation.

What I find fascinating is how far AI-assisted development can push projects like this. There's no way I'd have attempted something of this scale as a traditional solo side project.

It's still an early prototype. No missions, no NPCs, no police, and lots of room for improvement. But you can already explore the real planet on foot, by car, or by plane.

**Free, open source, and cross-platform (Linux, Windows, macOS).**

GitHub: [https://github.com/galatolofederico/gtw](https://github.com/galatolofederico/gtw)

I'd love feedback from other people experimenting with AI game development, especially about what features to tackle next or ways to improve the experience.

And of course, contributions and PRs are welcome!
